questions.question: When backing a truck, what should you do?

options.text: Rely on your mirrors to guide you.
Walk around the area first to check for obstacles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk around the area first to check for obstacles.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, walk around your vehicle to see the path and find any obstacles. Mirrors have blind spots, so you cannot rely on them alone. It is best to use a helper if possible.

questions.question: When you see a train approaching a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Try to cross the tracks quickly.
Stop and wait for the train to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait for the train to pass.
questions.explanation: Never try to beat a train across the tracks. It is hard to judge how fast a train is moving. Stop and wait for the train to pass before you cross.

questions.question: What is the only way to sober up after drinking alcohol?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wait.
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol from your body at a fixed rate. Cold showers and black coffee do not speed this up. Only time allows your body to remove alcohol from your system.

questions.question: What gauge shows the air pressure in your vehicle's air tanks?
questions.correctAnswerText: The supply pressure gauge
questions.explanation: Vehicles with air brakes must have a supply pressure gauge. This gauge tells you how much air pressure is in each air tank.

questions.question: On a slippery road, a driver should:

options.text: Make turns as quickly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid passing slower vehicles.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, drive slowly and smoothly. Make gentle turns and do not pass other vehicles unless necessary.

questions.question: After an accident, why should flares be used with caution?

options.text: Spilled fuel on the ground could catch fire.
Other drivers may not see the flares if it is sunny.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spilled fuel on the ground could catch fire.
questions.explanation: Vehicle fires after accidents often happen when flares are used near spilled fuel. Always use flares with caution.

questions.question: Why should you do routine vehicle inspections?
questions.correctAnswerText: To ensure safety.
questions.explanation: Regular inspections are most important to keep you and other road users safe.

questions.question: What can a broken exhaust system cause?

options.text: Poisonous fumes can enter the cabin.
It should not be a concern.

questions.correctAnswerText: Poisonous fumes can enter the cabin.
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system can let poisonous fumes into your vehicle's cabin. Check your exhaust system for loose, broken, or missing parts.

questions.question: If another driver is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: When being tailgated, increase the space between your vehicle and the one ahead. This reduces the need for sudden movements and gives the tailgater room to pass. Speeding up is not safe because the tailgater may follow at the higher speed, making it more dangerous.

questions.question: What must truck tractors with air brakes built after March 1, 1997 have?
questions.correctAnswerText: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS).
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997, must have anti-lock brakes.

questions.question: Eating while driving:

options.text: Is a good way to save time.
Takes the driver's attention off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Takes the driver's attention off the road.
questions.explanation: Eating while driving is dangerous. It takes your attention away from driving and requires you to take one hand off the steering wheel.

questions.question: When the spring brakes are on, you should never:
questions.correctAnswerText: Push down the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Never push the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. The combined force of the springs and air pressure can damage the brakes.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help prevent a truck from rolling over?

options.text: Keeping cargo as close to the ground as possible
Driving on the shoulder of a road

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving on the shoulder of a road
questions.explanation: To prevent a truck from rolling over, keep cargo weight low and drive slowly on turns. Driving on the shoulder does not help prevent rollovers.

questions.question: An after-trip inspection should be done:
questions.correctAnswerText: After every trip.
questions.explanation: Check your vehicle after every trip or at the end of each day. Complete a vehicle inspection report if required.

questions.question: ____ make up the emergency brake system.

options.text: Only parts of the parking brake system
Only parts of the service brake system
Parts of both the parking and service brake systems

questions.correctAnswerText: Parts of both the parking and service brake systems
questions.explanation: An air brake system has three types of brakes: service brakes, parking brakes, and emergency brakes. The emergency brake system uses parts from both the parking and service brake systems.

questions.question: Drivers stuck behind a slow-moving vehicle often:
questions.correctAnswerText: Follow too closely.
questions.explanation: Drivers often tailgate slow-moving vehicles. If someone tailgates you, let them pass safely.

questions.question: Texting while driving is especially dangerous because:

options.text: It distracts the driver mentally and physically.
A message may upset the driver.
People may become too focused on their phones.

questions.correctAnswerText: It distracts the driver mentally and physically.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is very dangerous. It takes your attention away from the road and requires you to remove at least one hand from the steering wheel.

questions.question: Brakes out of adjustment will:

options.text: Cause some brakes to work too hard and fail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cause some brakes to work too hard and fail.
questions.explanation: Out-of-adjustment brakes wear out faster than properly adjusted brakes. Check brake adjustment often to prevent brake problems.

questions.question: Antifreeze helps an engine run properly:

options.text: Only when it is cold outside.
In both cold and hot weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: In both cold and hot weather.
questions.explanation: Always keep enough water and antifreeze in your cooling system. Despite its name, antifreeze is helpful even in hot weather.

questions.question: To prevent a vehicle from rolling backward when starting from a stop, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Partly engage the clutch.
questions.explanation: For manual transmission vehicles, partly engage the clutch before releasing the brake pedal. This helps prevent the vehicle from rolling backward.
